B1.rationale: Relabel, not re-filter. The measured quantity is a SESSION return and the confound held fixed is the day-of-week effect of that session. Filtering on release weekday would admit 6 Good Friday releases whose returns are MONDAY returns into a comparison whose control group is pure Friday -- i.e. it would reintroduce exactly the weekday confound the restriction exists to remove. Both independent round-6 reviewers examined this rationale specifically and judged it sound rather than a device to avoid a re-run.

blockers.title: Friday estimand inconsistent with README claim
blockers.decision: RELABEL (keep the analysis, correct the prose). The verdict offered two routes; this is route (i) - Friday trading-session estimand, with the six Good Friday cases disclosed by name.
blockers.why_this_route: Route (ii) - filter on release weekday (243 events) plus weekday-matched controls - is internally coherent but statistically worse for the question actually being asked. The measured quantity is a SESSION return and the confound held fixed is the day-of-week effect OF THAT SESSION. Filtering on release weekday would place six Monday returns against a pure-Friday control group, reintroducing exactly the weekday contamination the restriction exists to remove. Route (i) is therefore not merely the cheaper fix, it is the correct one; the defect was purely in the labelling.
blockers.before: df['weekday'] held the SESSION weekday but the README described the filter as 'NFP released on a Friday'. 243 of 253 valid releases are dated a Friday; only 237 are traded in a Friday session. The 6-event gap was invisible in both code and prose.
blockers.after: Every event now carries release_date/release_weekday AND session_date/session_weekday plus a session_shifted_from_release flag. A new sample.friday_estimand block states the estimand, names all six Good Friday releases with their Monday sessions and their |return|, and records why session weekday is the correct filter. README rewritten throughout: the phrase now used is 'NFP absorbed in a Friday trading session'. A reconciliation assertion fails the run if release-Friday minus session-Friday no longer equals the shifted set, and a second invariant fails if a release ever changes weekday while itself being a trading day (i.e. if the mapping rule stops being 'same day, else next open').
blockers.numbers_note: 1.189x / p=0.0209 / n=237 are the same as before. This blocker was a claim-scope defect, not a computational one; nothing about the estimate moved because nothing about the computation changed.
blockers.independent_verification: All six confirmed as Good Friday (the only recurring Friday market holiday in April). Verified against the SPY session calendar: exactly 6 of the 254 selected releases are not trading days, and those 6 are precisely these dates. Release-weekday counts recomputed straight from the pinned ALFRED fixture: 244/254 selected are Friday, 243/253 among valid events - matching the verdict's figure of 243.

blockers.title: no multiplicity family declared while claiming 5% significance
blockers.decision: FIXED - confirmatory family declared, Holm reported under both that family and all 22 outputs, everything else marked exploratory, and every significance flag in the artifact mechanically stamped.
blockers.before: 22 p-values, no correction, no confirmatory/exploratory boundary, and a bare significant_5pct: true next to them.
blockers.after: A six-test confirmatory family (the tests README's methods line has named since before this rerun, and the only ones the published article draws directional claims from). Holm reported for that family AND for all 22 inferential outputs, presented side by side rather than selectively. Every statistical_tests / regime_analysis / time_trend / directional_bias / seasonal_analysis entry now carries a multiplicity stamp naming its family and both adjusted values; a new test added without a family assignment fails the run.
blockers.family_choice_justification: The six are the tests named in README's methods line, which predates the date correction and this rerun, and they are the only tests the online article makes directional claims from. They were NOT pre-registered - this is stated explicitly in the artifact (multiplicity.pre_registered = false), in the README, and here, and it is precisely why the all-outputs figure is reported alongside rather than the narrow family being presented as the only defensible reading.
blockers.holm_note: Holm rather than Romano-Wolf: the family mixes Welch t, Mann-Whitney U and two correlation statistics on overlapping samples, so no single resampling scheme is jointly valid for all four. Holm controls FWER under arbitrary dependence. Manufacturing a joint scheme to buy power would be the wrong trade in a correction specifically about overstatement.
blockers.verdict_estimate_reconciliation: The verdict estimated Holm ~0.0417 for the six-test family and ~0.375 for all 22. Computed independently here: 0.041703 and 0.375329, with the all-outputs family landing at exactly 22 members. Both match.
